delete.description: Removes the organization's staged GitHub App, with its installations and secrets, leaving its personal access token the live credential. A live App is refused; it is removed by disconnecting it. The App itself stays on GitHub, and the answer links to where it can be deleted.

get.description: Returns the organization's own GitHub App, the GitHub accounts it or the deployment's App is installed on, and whether GitHub delivers the App's webhooks here. The answer is read from stored state, and when the last webhook check is more than ten minutes old the read starts a new one with GitHub in the background.
get.summary: Get the organization's GitHub App status

post.description: Makes the organization's staged GitHub App its live credential and deletes its personal access token, after refreshing the App's installations from GitHub and checking it is installed on at least one account. Returns the App status as the switch leaves it.

get.description: Returns how many of the organization's tracked repositories its GitHub App's installations can reach, and which they cannot, so a switch from the token to the App would stop polling them. It first refreshes the App's stored installations from GitHub, and uses the stored ones when that fails.
get.summary: Preview switching to the GitHub App

post.description: Removes the organization's live GitHub App, with its installations and secrets, and clears its GitHub host unless a commit signer is on it, leaving the organization with no GitHub access until another credential is connected. A staged App is refused; it is discarded instead. The App itself stays on GitHub, and the answer links to where it can be deleted.

Connects a GitHub App that already exists to the organization, from its id and private key, after checking the pair, the App's permissions, and any client secret with GitHub. The App is staged while the organization's personal access token stays live, and is live at once otherwise; the answer is the App status with the permissions check beside it.

get.description: Returns the address of the page on the organization's GitHub where its own GitHub App is installed on a GitHub account.
get.summary: Get the GitHub App's install page

post.description: Asks GitHub which accounts the organization's GitHub App, or the deployment's App it is connected through, is installed on, updates the stored installations to match, and returns the same body as the App status read. GitHub refusing the App is recorded on the App and answered as an error that says what to do.

Asks GitHub to deliver again the newest 50 failed installation deliveries of the organization's own GitHub App, from the 30 days of deliveries GitHub keeps, and returns how many there were and how many GitHub accepted. GitHub makes the deliveries afterwards, and the next App status read checks the webhook again.
post.summary: Replay the GitHub App's failed installation webhooks

get.description: Returns the name and email address the organization's agents' commits carry, and whether and how they are signed, resolved the way an agent's commits are.
get.summary: Get who the organization's agents commit as

delete.description: Removes the organization's commit signer and deletes its private keys, and clears the organization's GitHub host when no other GitHub credential is on it. The public keys stay on the account until someone removes them on GitHub.

get.description: Returns the GitHub user account the organization's agents' commits are authored, committed, and signed as, with the public key Triage Factory signs with and the signer's status.

patch.description: Sets or clears the committer email address the signer's commits carry, and returns the signer with the change applied. GitHub's verified addresses for the account cannot be read, so a wrong address shows when a pushed commit fails GitHub's verification.

post.description: Looks up the GitHub user account on the organization's GitHub host, generates an SSH key pair, and registers the account as the organization's commit signer, pending until its key is verified. The answer carries the public key and the title to add it to the account under as a signing key.

Generates a new SSH key pair for the signer and returns it as the pending key, replacing any pending key an earlier rotation left. The current key keeps signing until a verify finds the new one on the account.
post.summary: Start rotating the commit signer's key

post.description: Looks for the signer's key among the account's signing keys on GitHub, or for a rotation's new key while one is under way, and for a broken signer checks the commit that broke it again. When the check passes the signer becomes active, and a rotation's new key, when it was the one found, replaces the old key, whose private half is deleted.
post.summary: Verify the commit signer's key on GitHub

get.description: Counts the repositories the organization's teams track on its GitHub host by whether its GitHub credential can read their Dependabot alerts, as polling last found them.
get.summary: Count Dependabot alert access on tracked repositories

post.description: Returns one page of the repositories the organization's GitHub App installations can reach that no team tracks, as the last installation refresh found them. It reads stored state and asks GitHub nothing.

items.description: The rows of this page, as an empty array when it has none.

next_page_token.description: The page_token that reads the next page, absent on the last page.

total_count.description: How many rows match the request's filters across every page, or null for a list whose upstream cannot count them.

post.summary: List repositories the GitHub App reaches untracked

post.description: Returns one page of the repositories a team tracks that the organization's GitHub App installations do not grant, as the last installation refresh found them, so they are not polled. It reads stored state and asks GitHub nothing.

items.description: The rows of this page, as an empty array when it has none.

next_page_token.description: The page_token that reads the next page, absent on the last page.

total_count.description: How many rows match the request's filters across every page, or null for a list whose upstream cannot count them.

post.summary: List tracked repositories the GitHub App cannot reach

get.description: Returns whether the caller has a GitHub account linked on the organization's GitHub host, its login, and whether the caller can link one by signing in to GitHub.
get.summary: Get the caller's linked GitHub account

post.description: Asks the organization's GitHub host which account the personal access token belongs to, links that account to the caller on that host, replacing any linked there before, and discards the token. Local mode only.
post.summary: Link the caller's GitHub account with a token

post.description: Starts connecting the organization to an installation of the deployment's GitHub App on the named GitHub account, and returns the GitHub authorization page the caller's browser must open to finish it. It sets a cookie the finish reads, expiring with the attempt. Multi mode only.

Disconnects the organization from every installation of the deployment's GitHub App it is connected to, leaving it with no GitHub access until another credential is connected. The installations stay on GitHub. Multi mode only.

Disconnects the organization from one installation of the deployment's GitHub App. Disconnecting the last one leaves the organization with no GitHub access, as the full disconnect does. The installation stays on GitHub. Multi mode only.

delete.description: Deletes the organization's GitHub personal access token, and clears its GitHub host unless a GitHub App or a commit signer is on it. An organization with no token gets the same answer.

put.description: Checks the personal access token with the organization's GitHub host and stores it as the organization's GitHub credential, replacing any token it had, then restarts GitHub polling under it. An organization with a GitHub App is refused; it switches through the App's switch route. Local mode only.

post.description: Checks the personal access token with GitHub and returns the account it authenticates as, how many of the organization's tracked repositories it can reach, and which it cannot. The token is not stored. Local mode only.

Checks the personal access token with GitHub, stores it as the organization's GitHub credential, and removes the organization's GitHub App, staged or live, with its installations and secrets. The App itself stays on GitHub, and the answer links to where it can be deleted. Local mode only.
post.summary: Switch from the GitHub App to a token

get.description: Asks the organization's GitHub host, through the organization's GitHub credential, for the account a login names, and returns its id and login.

parameters.description: The account's login on the organization's GitHub host, with a [bot] suffix for a bot.
parameters.name: login

get.summary: Look up a GitHub account by login

get.description: Asks the organization's GitHub host, through the organization's GitHub credential, for the account an id names, and returns its id and the login it has now.

post.description: Returns one page of the organization's Slack connections, active and inactive, ordered by workspace name, then workspace id, then app id. Each connection carries its Socket Mode status when it has one.

items.description: The rows of this page, as an empty array when it has none.

next_page_token.description: The page_token that reads the next page, absent on the last page.

total_count.description: How many rows match the request's filters across every page, or null for a list whose upstream cannot count them.

get.description: Returns the organization's LLM spend over the window, in USD, with its totals by team, person, category, model, and UTC day, and the spend attributed to no team.

parameters.description: Start of the window, inclusive, as an RFC 3339 timestamp or a YYYY-MM-DD date read as UTC midnight; with since and until both absent the window is the current UTC calendar month up to now, and with only one of them given the other end is open.
parameters.name: since

parameters.description: End of the window, exclusive, as an RFC 3339 timestamp or a YYYY-MM-DD date read as UTC midnight, which must be after since when both are given.
parameters.name: until

patch.description: Sets or clears the branch agents base their work on in the repository, and returns the repository with the change applied.

parameters.description: The repository's id in Triage Factory.
parameters.name: id

post.description: Returns one page of the tasks the caller can see, narrowed by the body's filters and ordered by sort_key, or without one by attention and then priority. Each task says whether the caller may write it. A page_token resumes after the last task of the page that returned it, and is refused for different filters.

items.description: The rows of this page, as an empty array when it has none.

next_page_token.description: The page_token that reads the next page, absent on the last page.

total_count.description: How many rows match the request's filters across every page, or null for a list whose upstream cannot count them.

delete.description: Removes a person from the team. A caller who names their own id leaves the team, and the team's last admin cannot be removed.

parameters.description: The id of the person to remove.
parameters.name: user_id

get.description: Returns the team's LLM spend over the window, in USD, with its totals by category, event handler, model, and UTC day. The totals by person are included only for a team admin.

parameters.description: The team's id, or default for the one team in local mode.
parameters.name: team_id

parameters.description: Start of the window, inclusive, as an RFC 3339 timestamp or a YYYY-MM-DD date read as UTC midnight; with since and until both absent the window is the current UTC calendar month up to now, and with only one of them given the other end is open.
parameters.name: since

parameters.description: End of the window, exclusive, as an RFC 3339 timestamp or a YYYY-MM-DD date read as UTC midnight, which must be after since when both are given.
parameters.name: until

get.description: Upgrades the connection to a websocket that streams events for the caller in their current organization, such as a changed task list or a run's new messages. Most events say only that a resource changed, and the client reads it again through its route.
